<content>1: ---
2: title: How to add analytics to your Next.js application
3: nav_title: Analytics
4: description: Measure and track page performance using Next.js Speed Insights
5: ---
6: 
7: {/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}
8: 
9: Next.js has built-in support for measuring and reporting performance metrics. You can either use the [`useReportWebVitals`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-report-web-vitals) hook to manage reporting yourself, or alternatively, Vercel provides a [managed service](https://vercel.com/analytics?utm_source=next-site&utm_medium=docs&utm_campaign=next-website) to automatically collect and visualize metrics for you.
10: 
11: ## Client Instrumentation
12: 
13: For more advanced analytics and monitoring needs, Next.js provides a `instrumentation-client.js|ts` file that runs before your application's frontend code starts executing. This is ideal for setting up global analytics, error tracking, or performance monitoring tools.
14: 
15: To use it, create an `instrumentation-client.js` or `instrumentation-client.ts` file in your application's root directory:
16: 
17: ```js filename="instrumentation-client.js"
18: // Initialize analytics before the app starts
19: console.log('Analytics initialized')
20: 
21: // Set up global error tracking
22: window.addEventListener('error', (event) => {
23:   // Send to your error tracking service
24:   reportError(event.error)
25: })
26: ```
27: 
28: ## Build Your Own
29: 
30: <PagesOnly>
31: 
32: ```jsx filename="pages/_app.js"
33: import { useReportWebVitals } from 'next/web-vitals'
34: 
35: function MyApp({ Component, pageProps }) {
36:   useReportWebVitals((metric) => {
37:     console.log(metric)
38:   })
39: 
40:   return <Component {...pageProps} />
41: }
42: ```
43: 
44: View the [API Reference](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/use-report-web-vitals) for more information.
45: 
46: </PagesOnly>
47: 
48: <AppOnly>
49: 
50: ```jsx filename="app/_components/web-vitals.js"
51: 'use client'
52: 
53: import { useReportWebVitals } from 'next/web-vitals'
54: 
55: export function WebVitals() {
56:   useReportWebVitals((metric) => {
57:     console.log(metric)
58:   })
59: }
60: ```
61: 
62: ```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
63: import { WebVitals } from './_components/web-vitals'
64: 
65: export default function Layout({ children }) {
66:   return (
67:     <html>
68:       <body>
69:         <WebVitals />
70:         {children}
71:       </body>
72:     </html>
73:   )
74: }
75: ```
76: 
77: > Since the `useReportWebVitals` hook requires the `'use client'` directive, the most performant approach is to create a separate component that the root layout imports. This confines the client boundary exclusively to the `WebVitals` component.
78: 
79: View the [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-report-web-vitals) for more information.
80: 
81: </AppOnly>
82: 
83: ## Web Vitals
84: 
85: [Web Vitals](https://web.dev/vitals/) are a set of useful metrics that aim to capture the user
86: experience of a web page. The following web vitals are all included:
87: 
88: - [Time to First Byte](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Time_to_first_byte) (TTFB)
89: - [First Contentful Paint](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/First_contentful_paint) (FCP)
90: - [Largest Contentful Paint](https://web.dev/lcp/) (LCP)
91: - [First Input Delay](https://web.dev/fid/) (FID)
92: - [Cumulative Layout Shift](https://web.dev/cls/) (CLS)
93: - [Interaction to Next Paint](https://web.dev/inp/) (INP)
94: 
95: You can handle all the results of these metrics using the `name` property.
96: 
97: <PagesOnly>
98: 
99: ```jsx filename="pages/_app.js"
100: import { useReportWebVitals } from 'next/web-vitals'
101: 
102: function MyApp({ Component, pageProps }) {
103:   useReportWebVitals((metric) => {
104:     switch (metric.name) {
105:       case 'FCP': {
106:         // handle FCP results
107:       }
108:       case 'LCP': {
109:         // handle LCP results
110:       }
111:       // ...
112:     }
113:   })
114: 
115:   return <Component {...pageProps} />
116: }
117: ```
118: 
119: </PagesOnly>
120: 
121: <AppOnly>
122:

167: ## Custom Metrics
168: 
169: In addition to the core metrics listed above, there are some additional custom metrics that
170: measure the time it takes for the page to hydrate and render:
171: 
172: - `Next.js-hydration`: Length of time it takes for the page to start and finish hydrating (in ms)
173: - `Next.js-route-change-to-render`: Length of time it takes for a page to start rendering after a
174:   route change (in ms)
175: - `Next.js-render`: Length of time it takes for a page to finish render after a route change (in ms)
176: 
177: You can handle all the results of these metrics separately:
178: 
179: ```js
180: export function reportWebVitals(metric) {
181:   switch (metric.name) {
182:     case 'Next.js-hydration':
183:       // handle hydration results
184:       break
185:     case 'Next.js-route-change-to-render':
186:       // handle route-change to render results
187:       break
188:     case 'Next.js-render':
189:       // handle render results
190:       break
191:     default:
192:       break
193:   }
194: }
195: ```
196: 
197: These metrics work in all browsers that support the [User Timing API](https://caniuse.com/#feat=user-timing).
198: 
199: </PagesOnly>
200: 
201: ## Sending results to external systems
202: 
203: You can send results to any endpoint to measure and track
204: real user performance on your site. For example:

I've updated the root page (`app/page.tsx`) to implement non-blocking analytics logging using the `after` function from `next/server`.

Here is the implementation details:
1.  **Non-blocking Logging:** Used `after()` to schedule the logging task to run after the response is sent to the client.
2.  **Request Data Access:** Accessed `headers()` *before* the `after` callback, as dynamic APIs cannot be called inside `after` within Server Components.
3.  **Simulation:** Added a mock `logPageView` function with a 2-second delay to demonstrate that the page load is not blocked by the logging operation.

You can verify this by running the development server (`npm run dev`) and checking the server console. You'll see the page load instantly, and the log message appear 2 seconds later.
